title: Nearly half of doctor posts empty at upazila health complexes
excerpt: Upazila health complexes have 6,288 of 13,036 doctor posts vacant, the state minister for health told parliament. Recruitment of 4,000 doctors has begun.

image.alt: The front of Birampur Upazila Health Complex in Dinajpur
image.credit: Wiki Ruhan / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Nearly half the doctor posts at upazila health complexes are vacant, State Minister for Health and Family Welfare MA Muhit told parliament this week, Prothom Alo reported. Of 13,036 sanctioned posts, 6,748 are filled and 6,288 are empty.

The minister answered on behalf of Health Minister Sardar Md. Sakhawat Hossain, who was absent. Across all government health facilities, 11,336 of 42,549 doctor posts are vacant, he said. Among third-class staff, including health workers, 21,656 of 57,306 posts are empty.

He also gave figures on the measles vaccination campaign: 21,791,259 children were vaccinated against a target of 18,015,064, or 121 percent. For private facilities, 8,273 licences were issued in the 2026-27 fiscal year, 250 facilities were fined or sealed, and about 500 were warned.

Recruitment of more than 4,000 doctors has begun, and newly recruited doctors will not be transferred out of upazila posts for two years, The Business Standard reported. Dengue tests are free at government hospitals, and community clinics are to become primary healthcare hubs, it said.

Why it matters

Upazila health complexes are the main public hospitals for rural people. When half the doctors are missing, patients turn to costly private care or to NGO clinics and community health workers. The figures come as the country faces long dengue and measles outbreaks that need rural staff on duty.

What to watch

How quickly the 4,000 new doctors are posted, whether the two-year rule keeps them in rural areas, and how the plan to turn community clinics into primary healthcare hubs involves NGOs that already run community health services.
